title: Pharmacophore-Guided Generative Design of Novel Drug-Like Molecules
experiments_summary: The study integrated a custom dual-objective reward function into the reinforcement learning generative model FREED++ to guide de novo molecule generation targeting estrogen receptor inhibitors for breast cancer. The reference set comprised 53 estrogen receptor antagonists and degraders. Molecules were encoded using two molecular representations: CATS (Chemically Advanced Template Search) descriptors for pharmacophore patterns and MACCS keys for substructural features. Pharmacophoric similarity was quantified via cosine similarity and Euclidean distance applied to CATS descriptors, while structural similarity was assessed using the Tanimoto coefficient on MACCS fingerprints and the MAP4 (MinHashed Atom-Pair fingerprint up to four bonds) metric. The reward function was designed to simultaneously maximize pharmacophoric similarity and minimize structural similarity to reference molecules, with weights of 1 assigned to QED and docking-related terms and 2 to pharmacophore and structural similarity metrics; all terms were min-max normalized per batch. Four reward configurations (Setups 1–4) combining different pairs of similarity metrics (Tanimoto+Euclidean, Tanimoto+Cosine, MAP4+Euclidean, MAP4+Cosine) were tested and compared against a baseline using QED scoring combined with docking via QVina. The fragment vocabulary and action space for FREED++ were constructed using Murcko scaffolds parsed from the ChemDiv database. Post hoc validation of generated molecules was performed by evaluating QED, synthetic accessibility (SA score), novelty, docking scores using QVina against the crystallographic structure of the alpha-estrogen receptor (PDB ID: 8AWG), and pharmacophoric and structural similarity metrics. Distributions of these properties across all setups were compared visually and quantitatively, with standard deviations reported. Computations were performed on a server with an NVIDIA A6000 GPU.
